[USER] The user has been meaning to organize their film journal.  
[USER] The user is looking for note-taking apps to help categorize and tag their entries.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended note-taking apps include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. **Evernote**: Allows creation of notebooks, tags, and stacks; supports images, audio, and video clips.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. **Notion**: An all-in-one workspace app for creating databases, tables, and pages; supports tags and filters.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. **Bear**: Minimalistic writing app with tags, folders, and notebooks; includes focus mode and word count goals.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. **Simplenote**: Lightweight app using tags and pins; simple and intuitive.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. **Trello**: Visual project management tool using boards, lists, and cards; can categorize films by genres, directors, etc.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. **Day One**: Journaling app with tags, photos, and audio recordings; allows setting reminders.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 7. **Quip**: Collaborative app for documents and spreadsheets; can create a film journal template.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 8. **OneNote**: Digital notebook app with sections, pages, and tags; integrates with Microsoft products.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested factors to consider when choosing an app: ease of use, customization, syncing, search and filtering, media support.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Encouraged the user to experiment with a few options for journaling.
